security_audit.summary: One finding confirms supply-chain exposure from the unpinned remote installation command. The other eighteen findings are Markdown identifiers, legitimate service links, or account authorization checks, not shell execution or system reconnaissance. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or malicious intent in the reviewed files; the hosted service was not assessed.

remediation.issue: The installation command executes an unpinned remote installer and selects an unpinned skill repository.
remediation.suggestion: Pin the installer version and immutable skill revision using supported syntax, and require review before running downloaded installation code.

content.value_statement: External tasks require finding compatible tools, checking access, and tracking results. This skill guides those steps through one connected ToolRouter MCP server.
actual_capabilities: Guide operation discovery and inspect live input schemas, prices, account requirements, and limitations.
Route web search, website extraction, and SEO tasks to available provider operations.
Guide image, video, and audio operations with budget checks and asynchronous status tracking.
Select company or economic data sources while retaining dates, units, and geography.
Guide authorized X and LinkedIn publishing after checking the connected account and current operation schema.
Check advertised credit and job status tools, then return source links, completed assets, or verified action results.
limitations: Requires a connected ToolRouter MCP server and any credentials required by the selected operation.
Provider references do not guarantee deployed operations or account access; client profiles may expose fewer tools.
Paid operations require an approved budget and sufficient credits; the skill does not supply either.
The skill provides workflow instructions, not local tool implementations; external providers control availability, coverage, and output quality.

use_cases.title: Compare Search and SEO Evidence
use_cases.description: Discover search and keyword operations, gather source links, and retain market, date range, and measurement limitations.

use_cases.title: Produce Approved Media Assets
use_cases.description: Find an available media operation, check its price, and track the job until completed asset links are available.

use_cases.title: Retrieve Company and Economic Data
use_cases.description: Select registry or statistical operations and report results with source dates, units, geography, and access limitations.

prompt_templates.title: Find an Available Search Tool
prompt_templates.prompt: Use my connected ToolRouter server to discover web search operations. Report available schemas and access requirements without executing paid operations.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: inspect available tools before choosing an operation.

prompt_templates.title: Research Keyword Demand
prompt_templates.prompt: Research keyword demand for electric bicycles in the United Kingdom through ToolRouter. Check schemas and prices, request spending approval, and retain provider limitations.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: gather SEO evidence for a defined market.

prompt_templates.title: Generate and Verify an Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate one square product image through an available ToolRouter operation, within my approved $2 budget. Verify job completion and return the asset link.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: coordinate paid media generation and asynchronous completion.

prompt_templates.title: Publish an Authorized Social Post
prompt_templates.prompt: Publish my approved launch text to the connected X account I specified. Verify its identity and operation schema; check uncertain status before retrying.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: perform an authorized write without duplicating uncertain actions.

output_examples.input: Discover search tools without spending credits.
output: Operation review: available schemas, account requirements, and prices are summarized before execution.
Execution status: no paid operation requested.

output_examples.input: Generate an image within the approved budget.
output: A completed result includes the asset link and verified job status.
A pending result reports the outstanding job, rather than claiming the image is ready.

output_examples.input: Retrieve economic data for a selected country.
output: The result identifies the statistical source, observation period, units, and country.
Coverage gaps and provider limitations remain visible alongside the retrieved values.

best_practices: Inspect the live operation schema, account access, and price before execution.
Keep credentials in the client credential store and confirm authority for account changes, publishing, and spending.
Track asynchronous jobs and verify uncertain writes before retrying or reporting success.
anti_patterns: Inventing operation names or treating provider listings as proof of account access.
Changing providers, connecting accounts, or spending credits without task authority.
Repeating uncertain writes or reporting queued jobs as completed results.

faq.question: Which assistants can use this skill?
faq.answer: The skill targets Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. The client must support the connected remote MCP server and its authentication flow.

faq.question: Does the skill work without ToolRouter?
faq.answer: No. It guides ToolRouter operations and requires a connected server exposing the needed tools.

faq.question: Are all listed providers available to my account?
faq.answer: No. Provider references describe integrations, while live schemas and your client profile determine available operations and account requirements.

faq.question: Can operations cost money?
faq.answer: Yes. Inspect operation prices and available credits, then obtain task-specific spending authority before paid execution.

faq.question: Can it publish to X or LinkedIn?
faq.answer: It guides supported publishing operations when available. Confirm the connected account, authorized content, and live schema before posting.

faq.question: How should credentials and installation be handled?
faq.answer: Keep tokens in the client credential store. Review downloaded installation code and prefer pinned installer versions and immutable skill revisions.
